correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Lyndon substrings by number of marked ones: singleton letters, 0^i1 for 1<=i<=max(a,b,c), two-one strings with strictly decreasing initial and internal zero runs, and three-one strings where i>max(b,c) or i=b>c. For every nonempty mixed Lyndon factor the first symbol is 0 and last is 1; its cyclic zero-run triple determines unique least rotation, excluding periodic ties. These disjoint counts give the exact formula including m=0 and adjacent 1s. Partition of (a,b,c) by six strict and six tie orders and a three-equal stratum generates the stated rational F; independently expanded its Q terms and compared every histogram coefficient m=0..15 against complete compositions (sum choose(m+3,3)). Independently directly tested all 715 words m<=9 using every substring/rotation, and separately recomputed six-sector Dirichlet rational moments. Uniform weak compositions converge to uniform simplex; the indicator terms vanish after /m. Finite tests corroborate the all-length proof and do not prove it by themselves.
residual_risks: Three ones only, ordered binary alphabet, contiguous distinct factors; no general fixed-weight theorem or piecewise CDF asserted. Coefficient checks are finite; proof supplies universal result.

value.rationale: The first weight-three binary-word family with genuine three-marker cyclic tie conditions receives a complete rational distribution (not just a scalar statistic) and a limiting six-sector law. This exact infinite sparse-slice structural invariant naturally complements established Lyndon-factor extremum and average questions; its moments and exact count are reusable typical-case benchmarks.
residual_risks: Restriction to three 1s; does not solve general marker-count distributions.

final_claim: For w=0^a1 0^b1 0^c1 0^d with a,b,c,d>=0, distinct contiguous Lyndon-factor count is 1+1_{m>0}+max(a,b,c)+(a-b)_++(b-c)_++(a-max(b,c))_++1_{a>=b>c}; a rational bivariate fixed-three-one histogram F(z,y)=y+y^2/(1-z)(Q(z,y)/(1-z^3y)-1+z) and six uniform-Dirichlet sector limit have mean 19/24, second moment 37/45 and variance 563/2880.
limitations: No general finite alphabet or positive-density ones limit; historical sparse-Lyndon literature not exhaustively covered; external Lean/expert status unchanged.
